cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's audit machine check HANGS Construction's cash. An audit is an independent check of the books.
First, materiality, the size of mistake that matters: $12,000. Cash agrees all through the books.
Next, a confirmation: the bank writes straight to the auditors. It reports $42,300, $12,400 more than the books.
A bank reconciliation matches the books to the bank statement. Four June payments had not cleared yet.
Then it follows each open item. One old check was never cashed, and a $700 bank fee was never recorded.
Cut-off: is each payment in the right year? Yes, and no cash is held back.
Last, it sets what it found against materiality and writes the workpapers for the CPA.

All done. The gap with the bank is fully explained. The one known mistake is the $700 bank fee, well under materiality. Eight items stay open, including the uncashed check and a reconciliation no one has reviewed. The CPA, a person, concludes and signs. The machine gives no opinion.
